@removeNamed: screen-reader name of the × button that takes a choice or a file out of a cell (it isn't deleted); {name} is the choice's or the file's name

property.@menuLabel: screen-reader name of the menu with a database property's settings; {name} is the property's name (a column like Status or Due)
property.@type: a property's type (Text, Number, Date…): a row in the property's settings that opens the list of types, and the back button at the top of that list (a noun)
property.name: Property name
property.@name: placeholder and screen-reader name of the box where a database property (a column) is named
property.@formula: heading above a formula property's expression in its settings menu
property.@writeFormula: shown in place of a formula property's expression while it has none; clicking opens the formula editor
property.@numberFormat: label of the menu that chooses how a number property's values are written (plain, with commas, percent, a currency)
property.@numberFormatOption: an option in the number format menu; {format} is the format's name (Percent, Dollar), {example} a number written that way (45%, $1,234.50)
property.@decimals: label of the menu that chooses how many digits a number property shows after the decimal point
property.@decimalsAuto: option in the Decimals menu: show as many decimal digits as the number has
property.@showAs: label of the switch that shows a number property's values as digits, a bar or a ring
property.@showNumbersAs: screen-reader name of that switch (digits, bar or ring)
property.@showAsBar: option of Show as: draw each number as a progress bar
property.@showAsRing: option of Show as: draw each number as a progress ring (a circle that fills up)
property.@fullAt: label of the box with the number at which a progress bar or ring is full (100 by default)
property.@showOnCalendar: label of a switch in a date property's settings: put its dates on the Calendar view (the app's calendar, as the Calendar view is named)
property.showOnCalendarSwitch: Show these dates on the Calendar
property.@buttonSays: label of the box with the text a button property's buttons show ("the button says…")
property.@whenClicked: heading above the list of what a button property does when someone clicks it
property.@prefix: label and screen-reader name of the box with the letters an ID property puts before each row's number (TASK in TASK-12)
property.@prefixExample: example shown in the empty Prefix box: letters an ID property could put before each row's number (TASK-12); write it as a short word in capitals
property.@description: placeholder of the box where a property gets a description, shown as a tooltip on its name
property.@descriptionLabel: screen-reader name of the box where a property gets a description
property.@filter: menu command (a verb) that starts a filter on this property in the view
property.@freeze: menu command in a table: keep every column up to and including this one in place while the rest scrolls sideways
property.freezeNoRoom: Not enough room to freeze through this column
property.@freezeNoRoom: why Freeze through this column can't be used: the frozen columns wouldn't fit in the table's width
property.@unfreeze: menu command in a table: let the frozen columns scroll again
property.@insertLeft: menu command: add a new property (a column) just before this one
property.@insertRight: menu command: add a new property (a column) just after this one

choices.heading: Choices
choices.@heading: heading above the list of options a select, multi-select or status property offers
choices.@colorOf: screen-reader name of the coloured dot that changes an option's colour; {name} is the option's name
choices.name: Choice name
choices.@name: screen-reader name of the box with an option's name
choices.@moveUp: command that moves an option one place up its list
choices.@moveDown: command that moves an option one place down its list
choices.@deleteNamed: screen-reader name of the × button that deletes an option from the property; {name} is the option's name
choices.@add: placeholder of the box at the end of the options list where a new option is typed
choices.@color: heading of the colours an option can have, and the screen-reader name of the panel of colours
choices.@search: placeholder of the box that filters a cell's options when new ones can't be added there
choices.@searchOrAdd: placeholder of the box at the top of a cell's options: typing filters them, Enter adds what's typed as a new option
choices.@typeFirst: placeholder of that box while the property has no options yet
choices.@editNamed: screen-reader name of the … button beside an option that opens its settings; {name} is the option's name
choices.@editTip: tooltip of that button: what its menu does
choices.@create: last row of a cell's options: makes a new option from what was typed. <pill> is the new option drawn as a coloured label; {name} is the typed text
choices.@edit: screen-reader name of the panel with one option's name, stage, colour and commands
choices.@stage: heading of the stages a status option can belong to (to do, in progress, complete)
choices.@deleteTitle: title of the dialog asking whether to delete an option that rows use; {name} is the option's name

deleteMessage.one: {count} row uses it and will be left empty here.
deleteMessage.other: {count} rows use it and will be left empty here.

choices.@deleteMessage: text of that dialog: {count} is the number of rows that have the option, which will be left without a value in this property

relation.@linksTo: label of the menu that chooses which database a relation property's rows link to
relation.@chooseDatabase: the first, unselectable entry of that menu while no database is chosen
relation.@thisDatabase: the database the property belongs to, in that menu (it can link to its own rows); {name} is the database's name
relation.@twoWay: label of the switch that makes a relation show in the linked rows too, when it links rows of the same database
relation.@twoWayShowOn: label of that switch when the relation links to another database; {name} is that database's name
relation.linkedAlsoShow: Linked rows also show this one in “{name}”.
relation.@linkedAlsoShow: note under the switch when it's on; {name} is the name of the property the linked rows show this row in
relation.@searchPlaceholder: placeholder of the box that finds rows to link a cell to; {database} is the linked database's name
relation.noDatabase: Pick which database this links to in the property’s settings.
relation.@noDatabase: shown in a relation cell's picker while its property doesn't link to a database yet
relation.@newRow: command at the end of the rows found: make a row with the typed text as its name in the linked database and link it; {title} is the typed text, {database} the database's name
relation.@noMatches: shown when no row's name matches what was typed
relation.@noRows: shown when the linked database is empty; {database} is its name

rollup.@relation: label of the menu that chooses which relation property a rollup sums up the linked rows of
rollup.@choose: the first, unselectable entry of that menu while no relation is chosen ("choose one")
rollup.@addRelationFirst: that entry when the database has no relation property to choose
rollup.@property: label of the menu that chooses which property of the linked rows a rollup works on
rollup.@countRows: entry of that menu: use no property, only count the linked rows
rollup.@calculate: label of the menu that chooses what a rollup works out (a sum, an average, a count…)

cell.@notANumber: message after typing into a number cell something that can't be read as a number; {text} is what was typed
cell.@noCourses: shown in a course cell's picker when there are no courses (school classes) to choose
cell.@newCourse: command in a course cell's picker that makes a new course (a school class)
cell.@missingFile: shown instead of a file's name when the file is no longer in the library
cell.@noFiles: shown in a files cell's picker while the cell has no files
cell.@addFromFiles: command in a files cell's picker that opens a chooser of files from the Files view (the app's file library, as the Files view is named)

value.@error: shown in a formula cell whose formula can't be worked out (the tooltip says why)
value.@openInBrowser: tooltip of a web address in a URL cell
value.@writeEmail: tooltip of an address in an email cell: clicking starts an email to it
value.@call: tooltip of a number in a phone cell: clicking calls it (a verb)

date.placeholder: Type a date: Friday, Oct 20, tomorrow 3pm…
date.@placeholder: placeholder of the box in the date picker where a date can be typed; the examples are things the box understands: a date with its weekday and month (Friday, Oct 20) and a day word with a time (tomorrow 3pm). It reads month names and the words for today, tomorrow and yesterday in English and in this language, so keep examples of that kind
date.@field: screen-reader name of a box where a date is typed or picked
date.@inAWeek: button in the date picker that picks the day a week from today
date.@thisMonth: button in the date picker's calendar that goes back to the current month
date.@endDate: label and screen-reader name of the switch that gives a date an end date, making it a range
date.@time: label of the switch that gives a date a time of day
date.@timeRange: the start and end times of a date range: <start/> and <end/> are the boxes with the times, <to>…</to> the word between them, drawn in grey
date.clickToSetStart: Click a day to set the start.
date.@clickToSetStart: hint under a date range's settings: the next day clicked in the calendar becomes the range's start
date.clickToSetEnd: Click a day to set the end.
date.@clickToSetEnd: hint under a date range's settings: the next day clicked in the calendar becomes the range's end

row.@properties: screen-reader name of the list of a database row's properties at the top of its page
row.templateBanner: This is a template. New rows made from it start with these values, this icon and everything written on this page.
row.@templateBanner: banner at the top of a database template's page; … marks the word drawn in bold
row.@useTemplate: button in that banner that makes a new row from the template
row.@empty: shown in place of a property's value when the row has none (a state, click to fill it in)
row.@addProperty: button under a row's properties that adds a property (a column) to the database, and the name of the list of types it opens
row.@hideEmpty: button under a row's properties that hides the properties without a value
row.@showEmpty: button that shows the hidden properties without a value again; {count} is how many are hidden

filter.@where: word at the start of a view's first filter, before the property and the test ("Where Status is Done")
filter.@and: word at the start of each further filter when rows must match all of them ("and Due is before today")
filter.@or: word at the start of each further filter when rows may match any of them ("or Due is before today")
filter.@property: screen-reader name of the menu that chooses which property a filter or a sort uses
filter.@deletedProperty: shown in that menu when the property a filter or sort used has been deleted
filter.@test: screen-reader name of the menu that chooses a filter's test (contains, is before, is empty…)
filter.@typeValue: placeholder of the box with the text a filter tests for
filter.@value: screen-reader name of the box with the text or number a filter tests for
filter.@aNumber: placeholder of the box with the number a filter compares with
filter.@days: after the test "is within the past" or "is within the next": <input/> is the box with the number of days, which picks the form (English keeps "days" for every number)
filter.@day: screen-reader name of the menu that chooses the day a date filter compares with (Today, Tomorrow, a date…)
filter.@chooseDay: the first, unselectable entry of that menu
filter.@exactDate: entry of that menu that shows a box to pick a fixed date
filter.@nothingToChoose: shown when a filter on choices, tags or linked rows has nothing to pick from
filter.empty: Show only the rows you need: “Status is Done”, “Due is within the next 7 days”…
filter.@empty: shown in a view's filter panel while it has no filters; the examples are filters on a Status and a Due property
filter.@match: screen-reader name of the switch between rows matching all of the filters or any of them
filter.@matchAll: option of that switch: rows must match every filter
filter.@matchAny: option of that switch: rows must match at least one filter

sort.@sortBy: words at the start of a view's first sort, before the property it sorts by
sort.@then: word at the start of each further sort, which orders rows that tie on the ones before ("then Due")
sort.@direction: screen-reader name of the switch between sorting up and sorting down
sort.@up: option of that switch, shown as an arrow: sort from the lowest or earliest value up (A to Z, 1 to 9)
sort.@down: option of that switch, shown as an arrow: sort from the highest or latest value down (Z to A, 9 to 1)
sort.@changePriority: screen-reader name of the button that swaps which of two sorts comes first
sort.@sortSecond: tooltip of that button on the first sort
sort.@sortFirst: tooltip of that button on a later sort
sort.empty: Rows are in your own order: drag them to rearrange. Add a sort to order them by a property instead.
sort.@empty: shown in a view's sort panel while it has no sorts
sort.@clear: command that removes every sort, so rows go back to the order they were dragged into
